reason: The pancreas can now respond to the rising blood glucose in the body.
expectation: The sensing cells will respond to the increased blood glucose, likely by releasing insulin.

reaction: The result matched my expectation and made the signal's destinations clear.
reason: Skeletal muscle is an indicated destination for the insulin signal and may respond by taking up glucose.
expectation: The muscle will respond to insulin by taking up more glucose from the blood.

effect: Insulin helped muscle take up glucose, and the goal now concerns keeping glucose available between meals.
reaction: The falling glucose and insulin insets clearly showed how the response changes.
reason: Time between meals should move the body into the situation described by the new goal.

expectation: Blood glucose will fall as cells continue using it between meals.

reaction: The result matched my expectation and points toward a stored fuel source.
reason: The pancreatic sensing cells may detect the falling glucose and start the response that keeps it available.
expectation: The pancreas will respond to falling blood glucose, likely by releasing glucagon.

alternatives.reason: The liver has stored fuel, though a pancreatic signal may come first.

effect: Falling blood glucose prompted glucagon release, with the signal travelling toward the liver.
reaction: The result matched my expectation and points to the liver's stored glycogen.
reason: The liver is the indicated destination for glucagon and contains stored glycogen.
expectation: The liver will respond by releasing glucose from its glycogen stores into the blood.

effect: The liver released glucose from glycogen, and the later reduction in glucagon showed how the response can ease as blood glucose rises. The chapter’s goals are complete.
reaction: The sequence brought the between-meals response together clearly.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting glucagon to the liver was most worthwhile because the result showed stored glycogen supporting blood glucose and the signal easing afterward.

leastWorthwhile.text: Connecting the meal’s glucose to the body first felt like a procedural step; the need for that order was not clear from the initial board.

surprise.text: I expected the pancreatic cells to respond directly to the glucose-rich blood, but the game first connected that blood to the body.

arbitrary.text: That initial ordering felt somewhat arbitrary, although the compatibility feedback resolved it without blocking progress.

continue.text: I would probably continue: the paired insulin and glucagon responses connected familiar organs to a useful feedback pattern, though the steps were fairly predictable.
